mathematical_reason: ProofWiki's formal simple-graph definition requires an irreflexive symmetric adjacency relation, equivalent to edges as unordered vertex doubletons. No multiple edges, loops or weights are allowed; finite V or nonempty V are optional restrictions, not general axioms.

ProofWiki's multigraph definition explicitly makes the edge collection a multiset of unordered two-element vertex subsets, allowing multiple copies of the same edge. Unlike a graph with loops, doubleton edges have distinct endpoints. A simple graph is the multiplicity-at-most-one special case.
